primary.key: Thee, Agni, have the Adityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue. They who love offerings cling to thee at solemn rites: by thee the Gods devour the duly offered food.
primary.s: In the book’s opening hymn, which names Agni as each god in turn, this verse turns to the gods; Sāyaṇa, on 2.1.13, reads them as eating and tasting only through Agni, waiting on him since without him they cannot eat the oblation.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.1.13, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400202 (2024)

basis.words: त्वन्मुखेनैव भक्षयंति त्वज्जिहयैवास्वादयंतीत्यर्थः । तथा त्वामेव रातिषाचः । रातिर्दान दत्तं हविरादि धनं वा। तेन समवेता देवा अध्वरेषु यज्ञेषु सश्चिरे । सेवंत त्वामेव प्रतीक्षंते विना त्वया स्वेषां हविर्भक्षणायोगात्
basis.gloss: The meaning is: they eat through thy mouth alone, they taste through thy tongue alone. So too the rātiṣācaḥ (rāti is a gift, the oblation or wealth given; the gods joined with it) attend thee at the adhvaras, the sacrifices: they serve and wait for thee alone, since without thee they cannot eat their oblation.

standby.key: Between both races, Agni, Sage, well skilled thou passest to and fro, As envoy friendly to mankind.
standby.s: In a short hymn offering Agni a kindling log, the verse precedes the call to sit on the sacred grass; Sāyaṇa, on 2.6.7, reads him as going into people’s hearts, knowing the births of worshippers and gods, as a king’s envoy learns his subjects’ minds.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.6.7, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 196891 (2019)

basis.words: हे कवे मेधाविन्नग्ने अंतर्जनानां हृदय ईयसे हि । गच्छसि जानासि वा। … उभया उभयविधानि जन्म जन्मानि यष्टॄणां यजमानानां यष्टव्यानां देवानां च संबंधीनि विद्वान् जानन् सन् … स यथा प्रजानां चित्तवृत्तिज्ञानाय राज्ञा प्रेरितस्तासां मनो जानाति तद्वत् त्वमप्यस्माकमंतरीयस इत्यर्थः
basis.gloss: O Kavi, wise Agni, thou goest within, into the heart of people: thou goest, or thou knowest. … Knowing the births of both kinds, those of the sacrificers who worship and those of the gods who are worshipped … As an envoy sent by the king to learn the thoughts of his subjects knows their minds, so thou too goest within us: that is the meaning.

primary.key: Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not. He sweeps away, like birds, the foe’s possessions. Have faith in him, for He, O men, is Indra.
primary.s: In a hymn whose refrain names Indra to the people, this verse meets those who doubt him; Sāyaṇa, on 2.12.5, reads the doubters as people who, not seeing him, think him nowhere, and the verse as bidding trust that Indra is, though not plainly seen.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.12.5, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401594 (2024)

basis.words: अपश्यंतो जना घोरं शत्रूणां घातकं यं पृच्छंति स्म कुह सेति । स इंद्रः कुत्र वर्तत इति … न क्वचिदसौ तिष्ठतीति मन्यमाना जना एनमिंद्रमाहुः एष इंद्रो नास्तीति … तस्माद् श्रदस्मा इंद्राय धत्त। स इंद्रोऽस्तीति विश्वासमत्र कुरुत । यद्यप्यसौ विशेषतोऽस्माभिर्न दृश्यते तथापि अस्तीति विश्वासं कुरुत
basis.gloss: People who do not see him ask of the terrible one, the slayer of foes, ‘Where is he?’, that is, where does Indra dwell … Thinking ‘he stays nowhere’, people say of Indra ‘this Indra is not’ … Therefore put faith in this Indra: have trust here that Indra is. Even though he is not distinctly seen by us, still have trust that he is.

standby.key: HE who, just born, chief God of lofty spirit by power and might became the Gods’ protector, Before whose breath through greatness of his valour the two worlds trembled, He, O men, is Indra.
standby.s: The verse opens a hymn that tells deed after deed under a refrain naming their doer as Indra; Yāska, Nirukta 10.10, reads it as the delight of a seer who had seen what he speaks of, joined to a narrative.
standby.src: Yāska, Nirukta 10.10, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

basis.words: at whose power even heaven and earth trembled on account of the greatness of liis might, i. e. on account to of the mightiness of his power. He, O men, is Indra. Thus the gratification of the seer wlio had an intuitive insight into reality expresses itself conjoined with a narrative.
basis.gloss: (Yāska, glossing the verse:) at whose power even heaven and earth trembled because of the greatness of his might, that is, of the mightiness of his power: he, O men, is Indra. Thus the delight of the seer who had seen the matter for himself (dṛṣṭārtha) expresses itself joined with a narrative (ākhyāna).
